newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP likely to apply for bank licence.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP likely to apply for bank licence.

text.p: Australia's largest insurance and pension fund group, the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), said it was likely to apply to the Reserve Bank of Australia for a banking licence.

AMP chief executive George Trumbull said in a television interview broadcast on Channel Nine's Business Sunday programme that AMP's Priority One home mortgage lending unit was most likely to be the vehicle for an AMP bank.
"We could go and are likely to go to the Reserve Bank and ask for a banking licence," Trumbull said.
"I mean that's pretty likely and I've been pretty consistent about that and Priority One is certainly well enough capitalised," he said.
"My guess is if we go to the Reserve Bank it will be for the AMP Bank."

Trumbull has previously said AMP was unlikely to buy an existing major bank outright as the route into banking, despite Treasurer Peter Costello's easing of the "Six Pillars" policy last week allowing insurance groups to merge with the big banks.
Trumbull said he saw a relatively short timetable for AMP's application for a banking licence.
He said he thought the government was likely to look at passing legislation allowing financial holding companies, which would be necessary for an insurance group to take on a banking arm.
Although AMP could get an exemption in the same way that Colonial Mutual did to acquire State Bank of New South Wales, he said.
